chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Bashshar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who indicates (shows) the houses and the estates, and takes the fee for it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is a remuneration (fee), there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا: There is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to charge a fee for showing houses or real estate in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (AS) validates the permissibility of 'ujrah' (brokerage fee) for guiding clients to properties, affirming it as a legitimate compensation for service. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that payment for facilitating transactions is lawful provided it is for the actual service rendered, distinguishing it from interest-based gains. It highlights the practical application of trade ethics in early Islamic society, where real estate and agricultural estate management were common commercial activities.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Bashhar, 
from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the man who indicates upon the houses and the places, and he takes the (finder’s)  fee upon it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a renumeration. There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ibn al-Bashshar who has said the following: “About the case of a broker who shows houses and assets for a certain amount of fee, abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said it is not unlawful.’”
